elements.element: Customer owns every Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause expressly states that Customer exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer.

elements.element: Customer owns all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The clause addresses Deliverables only; it does not mention work product or establish that all work product is included within Deliverables.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all rights in every Deliverable created for Customer.
elements.evidence: Vendor irrevocably assigns all right, title, interest, and intellectual property rights in each Deliverable upon creation.

elements.element: Vendor assigns to Customer all rights in all work product created for Customer.
elements.evidence: The assignment covers each Deliverable but does not expressly cover other work product.

elements.element: Vendor retains ownership of its pre-existing intellectual property.
elements.evidence: Vendor Technology is excluded from the assignment, but the clause neither states that Vendor owns it nor establishes that Vendor Technology encompasses all pre-existing Vendor IP. Section 14.3 was not provided.

elements.element: Vendor grants Customer a licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: The clause merely refers to a licence in Section 13.2. It does not establish the grantee, operative grant, or that the licence covers all Vendor IP embedded in Deliverables.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: The operative text expressly identifies the Section 13.2 licence applicable to Vendor Technology as perpetual.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: Only the assignment is described as irrevocable; the referenced licence is not.

elements.element: The licence to Vendor intellectual property embedded in the Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: No royalty-free term is stated for the referenced licence, and Section 13.2 was not provided.

elements.element: Customer retains all rights in Customer Data.
elements.evidence: Customer Data is not addressed.

elements.element: The ownership arrangement creates no joint ownership.
elements.evidence: Customer's ownership of each Deliverable is expressly exclusive, and Vendor Technology is separately carved out rather than jointly owned.

elements.element: Vendor owns its generic tools.
elements.evidence: The clause does not mention generic tools or establish that they fall within Vendor Technology.

elements.element: Vendor owns its know-how.
elements.evidence: The clause does not mention know-how or affirm Vendor ownership of it.

elements.element: Customer receives a licence or a substantively greater entitlement to the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Customer receives exclusive ownership and an assignment of all rights in each Deliverable, which is substantively greater than a licence as to the assigned Deliverable rights.

elements.element: Customer's entitlement to the Deliverables is perpetual.
elements.evidence: Ownership vests upon creation without an expiration, reversion, or term limitation.

elements.element: Customer's entitlement to the Deliverables is irrevocable.
elements.evidence: The assignment is expressly irrevocable.

elements.element: Customer's entitlement to the Deliverables is worldwide.
elements.evidence: The assignment transfers all right, title, interest, and intellectual property rights without a territorial limitation.

elements.element: Customer's entitlement to the Deliverables is royalty-free.
elements.evidence: Customer receives unqualified ownership of the assigned Deliverable rights rather than a royalty-bearing right to use them.

elements.element: Customer may use the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Exclusive ownership of all assigned intellectual property rights necessarily permits Customer to use the Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may modify the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: Assignment of all intellectual property rights gives Customer the greater right to modify and create derivative versions of the Deliverables.

elements.element: Customer may sublicense the Deliverables.
elements.evidence: As owner of the assigned Deliverable rights, Customer may grant licences to third parties, which is substantively greater than a sublicense right.

elements.element: Customer may exercise its Deliverable rights for its business.
elements.evidence: Customer's ownership is not restricted by purpose and therefore permits exercise for its business.

result.reason: The redline establishes strong Customer ownership and assignment rights in Deliverables, but it does not cover all work product or Customer Data and does not establish an irrevocable, royalty-free licence to embedded Vendor IP. The fallback also fails because Vendor ownership of generic tools and know-how is not stated or demonstrable from the undefined Vendor Technology carveout. References to unavailable Sections 13.2 and 14.3 cannot establish their omitted terms. The drafting otherwise preserves unrelated terms and does not create joint ownership, but it reaches neither complete level and relies materially on unseen cross-references.
